papers.full_text: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute respiratory illness and severe outcomes in older adults. Objective This retrospective cohort study investigated the health and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among adults ≥ 60 years in Japan. Methods Data were collected between 1 September 2008 and 31 August 2021 from the Medical Data Vision (MDV) hospital-based claims database and the insurance-based JMDC database. We investigated RSV-related complications during the first episode. Healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs were compared between baseline (pre-event: 30-day average costs during the 365 days before RSV diagnosis) and post-event (30 days after RSV diagnosis); differences were explored using paired sample t-tests (p < 0.05). Results A total of 178 cases identified between 2009 and 2019 were included in the study, 144 were from the MDV database (mean age 74 years) and 34 from the JMDC database (mean age 64 years). RSV-related complications were recorded in 61.1% and 55.9% of the MDV and JMDC cohorts, respectively. HCRU in the MDV cohort increased significantly from pre- to post-event (average number of outpatient visits per case: 1.21 to 2.07; average number of hospitalizations per case: 0.07 to 0.37), resulting in significant additional medical costs of ¥196,231 (p < 0.001). Conclusions Medically attended RSV infections were associated with substantial short-term increases in HCRU and total medical costs among older adults in Japan. These findings may help inform prevention strategies for severe RSV disease. | Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was associated with substantial short-term increases in healthcare resource utilization and medical costs among medically attended older adults in Japan, particularly during the first 30 days following diagnosis. | | These findings may help inform RSV prevention strategies, including vaccination. | 1 Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common virus affecting individuals of all ages, the most vulnerable being young children and older adults [1]. RSV can lead to severe infections such as pneumonia in older adults, especially those with chronic cardiovascular disease, pulmonary conditions, or diabetes [1,2,3]. Severe RSV infections may require hospitalization or non-invasive ventilation [1]. RSV is associated with lower and upper respiratory tract disease (LRTD/URTD), potentially leading to inflammatory responses that can cause complications such as exacerbation of asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and heart failure [2]. In Japan, the incidence and disease burden of RSV in older adults is likely underestimated due to the lack of routine testing and surveillance. A prospective study estimated that RSV infection occurs in 2.4% of ambulatory older adults in Japan [4]. A recent meta-analysis using 1999–2020 data from high-income countries estimated approximately 700,000 RSV-related acute respiratory infection (ARI) cases, 63,000 hospitalizations, and 4500 in-hospital deaths annually in older adults in Japan [5]. The economic burden of RSV in older adults in Japan is not well documented, but the costs of hospitalization due to RSV contribute considerably to this burden [6]. In 2023, RSV vaccines were approved for individuals aged ≥ 60 years in the USA, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and Japan [7,8,9]. In Japan, the indication was subsequently expanded to include adults aged 50–59 years in 2024 and 18–49 years in 2026, if they were diagnosed with a medical condition that put them at increased risk for severe RSV, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or asthma.[10]. However, there are currently no specific treatments, highlighting a considerable unmet medical need and the importance of vaccination, especially given the high proportion of Japan’s population that is aged > 65 years (30% in 2022) [11]. Understanding the real-world impact of RSV is essential. Estimating its clinical and economic consequences is key to informing optimal vaccination strategies. We conducted a retrospective analysis using data from two administrative claims databases to explore the disease and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among older adults in Japan. 2 Materials and Methods 2.1 Study Design In this retrospective observational cohort study, we investigated the health and economic burden associated with RSV infection among older adults (≥ 60 years) in Japan from 1 September 2008 to 31 August 2021 (Supplementary Fig. 1). Data from two commercially available administrative databases ensured diverse population coverage: a hospital-based database (Medical Data Vision Co. Ltd. [MDV]; Tokyo, Japan) and an insurance-based database (JMDC Inc. Payer). The MDV is an anonymized health claims database including Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination data covering lump-sum payments for acute-care hospital inpatient costs; as of data analysis, it comprises data for approximately 45 million patients and 35% of the data are from cases aged more than 65 years [12]. The JMDC is an anonymized employer-based health insurance claims database with more than 130 payers, covering inpatient, outpatient, and medication-dispensing services, in addition to annual health-check results; as of data analysis, it stores data of 12 million patients among which 2% are aged 65–74 years [13]. The study complied with all applicable privacy laws. It was out of scope of the Ethical Guidelines for Life Sciences and Medical Research Involving Human Subjects in Japan. We assessed identification periods, which were 1-year cycles (September to August), between 2009 and 2020, accounting for the 12-month baseline and follow-up periods (Supplementary Fig. 1). An index event was defined as the first eligible claim with a diagnostic code for RSV within each 1-year cycle. 2.2 Cases and Case Definitions RSV cases were defined as those having at least one RSV diagnosis claim, based on the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th Revision (ICD-10 codes: B34.8 [RSV infection only], J12.1, J20.5, or J21.0) [6, 14], during the identification period. The first RSV diagnosis within each 1-year cycle was included from the MDV (aged ≥ 60 years) or JMDC (aged 60–74 years) at the time of the index event. Cases with associated LRTD/URTD were defined, based on the relevant ICD-10 codes (URTD: B34.8, J00, J01.0–J01.4, J01.9, J02.0, J02.8–J03.0, J03.8–J04.2, J05.0, J05.1, J06.0, J06.8, J06.9, J30.0–J30.4, J34.0–J34.3, J34.8, J36, J38.0, J38.3, J38.4, J38.7, J39.0–J39.2, J39.8; LRTD: J11.0, J12.0, J12.1, J12.2, J12.3, J12.8, J12.9, J13, J14, J15.0–J16.0, J18.0–J18.2, J18.8, J18.9, J20.0–J21.1, J21.9, J22, J40, J44.0, J44.1, J68.0, J69.0, J69.1, J69.8, J70.2, J98.0, J98.2). The index date for RSV cases was derived using database-specific algorithms incorporating available information such as treatment start or hospital admission dates, claim month/year, and inpatient/outpatient service dates recorded in the same month to estimate the diagnosis date. Prediagnosis healthcare seeking was captured one week prior to the index date, and complications were recorded from one week prior until two weeks post index date. Comorbidities were recorded for a 12-month baseline period. Comorbidities of interest were selected based on RSV risk factors and conditions. 2.3 Endpoints Study objectives were to describe the disease and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among older adults in Japan. The baseline characteristics of older adults with RSV in the 12-month pre-event were described to enhance the understanding of the hidden disease burden. During the post-event period, we analyzed the overall incidence of the first RSV episode, the proportion of cases with associated LRTD/URTD, and RSV-related complications. To measure the incremental healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs associated with acute RSV infection, as well as the long-term effects of RSV on HCRU and medical costs, we compared HCRU (mean number of individual outpatient visits and hospitalizations, mean frequency of radiography and oxygen inhalation procedures) and direct medical costs (by age groups [60–74 versus ≥ 75 years], LRTD/URTD, and comorbidities) during three pre-defined timeframes (differences between pre-events and post-events): Period I, 30 days; Period II, 180 days; and Period III, 365 days [15]. 2.4 Statistical Analysis The overall incidence of the first RSV episode was calculated based on the number of cases with at least one RSV event during the study period divided by the sum of person-time at risk, expressed per 1000 person-years with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The MDV cohort was stratified into age groups (60–74 years and ≥ 75 years). Cases were further stratified into LRTD (LRTD ± URTD), URTD (URTD only), and baseline comorbidities (cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic renal failure, and pulmonary conditions) subgroups. Baseline characteristics, clinical outcomes, and duration of hospitalization were analyzed descriptively. The mean numbers of outpatient visits and hospitalizations, as well as medical costs, were compared between the pre-event period (12-month baseline average) and post-event period, the latter including the index date, with an aggregate analysis of the entire study period. Given the large sample size, the use of parametric methods was considered appropriate based on the central limit theorem [16]. Comparisons were analyzed using a paired sample t-test, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. For detailed information regarding the study design, sample size calculation, eligibility criteria, ICD-10 coding algorithms, variables, and data analysis, please see Supplementary Methods. 3 Results 3.1 Baseline Characteristics A total 144 RSV cases were identified in the MDV (60–74 years, n = 77; ≥ 75 years, n = 67) and 34 in the JMDC (60–74 years, n = 34) (Table 1, Supplementary Fig. 1). No RSV case was identified during the 2009–2010 year cycle. The highest count of RSV cases was identified in 2017–2018, with 44 cases (MDV: 38; JMDC: 6). Overall, the number of RSV cases increased over the study period and reached 38 and 36 RSV cases in 2018–2019 and 2019–2020, respectively. The mean (standard deviation, SD) age of the RSV cohorts was 74.5 (9.1) and 64.0 (3.6) years in the MDV and JMDC, respectively (Table 1). Most MDV RSV cases (58%) were treated in large hospitals (> 500 beds). The largest proportion of JMDC RSV cases (47%) were treated in small institutions (0–19 beds) (data not shown). The comorbidity burden, described using the median modified Charlson comorbidity index (mCCI), was 5 and 1 in the MDV and the JMDC cohorts, respectively (Table 1). Comorbidities were defined at baseline assessment and were present in 93–94% of RSV cases, with the most common being type 2 diabetes, followed by heart failure, hypertension, solid tumor malignancies, chronic liver failure, asthma, and COPD. From 2009 to 2019, the overall incidence rate for the MDV RSV cohort was 0.007 per 1000 person-years (95% CI 0.006–0.008). Due to the limited number of RSV cases recorded in the JMDC and the age limitation to 60–74 years, our subsequent analysis focuses on RSV cases recorded in the MDV. For further details about the JMDC cases, please see Supplementary Tables. 3.2 Complications RSV complications were identified from one week prior to and the 2-week period following the date of the first confirmed diagnosis of RSV. Further details are in Supplementary Methods, variables section 6. All RSV cases had LRTD or URTD (or both) associated with their first episode (Table 1). LRTD (with or without URTD) was observed in 78.5% and 58.8% of RSV cases in the MDV and JMDC cohorts, respectively. RSV-related complications were recorded in 61.1% (MDV) and 55.9% (JMDC) (Table 2). Frequent complications included heart failure, pneumonia, bronchitis, and respiratory failure. Exacerbation of asthma, in those with a prior diagnosis of asthma, occurred in 25.0% (MDV) and 20.0% (JMDC). Exacerbation of COPD was recorded in 18.8% of MDV cases with prior COPD, while no cases were recorded in the JMDC cohort. 3.3 Healthcare Resource Utilization Overall, HCRU in the MDV cohort was numerically higher during the post-event period for all timeframes (30, 180, and 365 days) (Fig. 1A, Supplementary Table 1). The average numbers of outpatient visits and hospitalizations per patient were significantly higher within the 30-day post-event period compared with the pre-event period (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event for the average number of outpatient visits was 1.21 [1.50] versus 2.07 [2.30]; for the average number of hospitalizations, it was 0.07 [0.12] versus 0.37 [0.51]; p < 0.001) (Fig. 1A). This impact decreased during the 180- and 365-day post-event periods, with no statistical significance detected in the 365-day post-event period. Similarly, the average number of outpatient visits per JMDC patient increased significantly, by 1.44 in the 30-day post-event period compared with the pre-event period (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event, 2.15 [2.49] versus 3.59 [2.86]; p < 0.001) (Supplementary Table 1). Simple radiography and oxygen inhalation were the two most common treatment procedures, with statistically significant increased use in the MDV cohort post-event across all study periods (Supplementary Table 1). 3.3.1 HCRU by Age Group In the MDV cohort, average outpatient visits and hospitalizations significantly increased post-event in both the 60–74 years (n = 77) and ≥ 75 years (n = 67) age groups (Table 3A). 3.3.2 HCRU by LRTD/URTD Subgroup Among MDV RSV cases with LRTD (n = 113), the average number of outpatient visits per case increased significantly by 0.8 when comparing 30-day periods pre- and post-event (pre-event mean [SD] versus post-event mean [SD]: 1.12 [1.24] versus 1.92 [2.15]; p < 0.001), and the average number of hospitalizations per case also increased significantly, by 0.34 (0.07 [0.10] versus 0.41 [0.53]; p < 0.001). Similarly, among MDV RSV cases with URTD (n = 31), outpatient visits per case increased significantly by 1.07 (1.54 [2.21] versus 2.61 [2.78]; p = 0.048) and hospitalizations per case by 0.14 (0.09 [0.16] versus 0.23 [0.43]; p = 0.039) (Table 3B). 3.3.3 HCRU by Comorbidities For MDV RSV cases with type 2 diabetes (n = 88), pulmonary conditions (n = 52), and cardiovascular conditions (n = 75), the number of outpatient visits per case increased significantly by 0.95 (1.36 [1.55] versus 2.31 [2.65]; p < 0.001), 0.60 (1.15 [0.85] versus 1.75 [1.34]; p < 0.001), and 0.89 (1.40 [1.63] versus 2.29 [2.76]; p = 0.002), respectively, during the first 30 days post-event compared with the pre-event period (Table 3C). The number of hospitalizations per case significantly increased among patients with type 2 diabetes (n = 88) by 0.30 (0.08 [0.13] versus 0.38 [0.53]; p < 0.001), among patients with pulmonary conditions (n = 52) by 0.26 (0.07 [0.12] versus 0.33 [0.47]; p < 0.001), among patients with cardiovascular conditions (n = 75) by 0.39 (0.10 [0.14] versus 0.49 [0.53]; p < 0.001), and among patients with chronic renal failure (n = 23) by 0.28 (0.11 [0.16] versus 0.39 [0.50]; p = 0.010) (Table 3C). 3.4 Cost Analysis In the MDV cohort, average costs in the first 30 days post-event significantly increased by Japanese yen (¥) 196,231.7, compared with the pre-event period (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event costs: ¥132,109.7 [¥230,165.4] versus ¥328,341.4 [¥526,699.1]; p < 0.001), primarily driven by a ¥187,256.0 increase in inpatient hospitalization costs (¥89,544.9 versus ¥276,800.9; p < 0.001 (Fig. 1B, Supplementary Table 2). 3.4.1 Costs by Age Groups In the MDV cohort, elevated HCRU significantly increased costs across age groups. In the 60–74 years group, costs increased by ¥122,552.2 (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event costs: ¥142,653.0 [¥268,553.5] versus ¥265,205.2 [¥515,195.5]; p = 0.012) (Table 3A). For those aged ≥ 75 years, costs increased by ¥280,908.1 (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event costs: ¥119,992.8 [¥177,354.1] versus ¥400,900.9 [¥534,248.5]; p < 0.001), driven by a ¥270,903.9 increase in inpatient costs (¥87,884.1 versus ¥358,788.0; p < 0.001) (Table 3A). 3.4.2 Costs by LRTD/URTD Subgroups For MDV RSV cases with LRTD (n = 113), post-event costs were higher than pre-event by ¥234,250.6 (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event period: ¥117,484.3 [¥222,607.4] versus ¥351,734.9 [¥562,674.5]; p < 0.001), driven by a significant increase in inpatient costs (¥84,476.6 versus ¥309,533.7; p < 0.001) (Table 3B). Outpatient costs did not significantly increase. For MDV RSV cases with URTD (n = 31), total costs increased by ¥57,646.7 post-event, but this was not statistically significant (Table 3B). 3.4.3 Costs by Comorbidities For MDV RSV cases with chronic renal failure, cardiovascular conditions, type 2 diabetes, or pulmonary conditions, the total medical costs increased by ¥251,060.2, ¥267,994.7, ¥175,618.8, and ¥150,362.9 in the 30 days post-event period, respectively, primarily due to increased inpatient admission costs. Inpatient costs for cardiovascular conditions and type 2 diabetes increased by ¥264,880.7 and ¥171,005.5 (both p < 0.001), respectively. Inpatient costs for chronic renal failure increased by ¥250,977.4 (p = 0.010) (Table 3C). 4 Discussion This is among the first studies describing the clinical and economic burden of RSV infections in older adults in Japan, for 11 yearly cycles from September 2009 to August 2020. The data provided broad population coverage, enabling subpopulation analysis and cross-validation of age-standardized outputs. Independent analyses of the JMDC and MDV databases offered complementary information across diverse healthcare settings. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute respiratory illness and severe outcomes in older adults. Objective This retrospective cohort study investigated the health and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among adults ≥ 60 years in Japan. Methods Data were collected between 1 September 2008 and 31 August 2021 from the Medical Data Vision (MDV) hospital-based claims database and the insurance-based JMDC database. We investigated RSV-related complications during the first episode. Healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs were compared between baseline (pre-event: 30-day average costs during the 365 days before RSV diagnosis) and post-event (30 days after RSV diagnosis); differences were explored using paired sample t-tests (p < 0.05). Results A total of 178 cases identified between 2009 and 2019 were included in the study, 144 were from the MDV database (mean age 74 years) and 34 from the JMDC database (mean age 64 years). RSV-related complications were recorded in 61.1% and 55.9% of the MDV and JMDC cohorts, respectively. Conclusions Medically attended RSV infections were associated with substantial short-term increases in HCRU and total medical costs among older adults in Japan. These findings may help inform prevention strategies for severe RSV disease. | Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was associated with substantial short-term increases in healthcare resource utilization and medical costs among medically attended older adults in Japan, particularly during the first 30 days following diagnosis. | | These findings may help inform RSV prevention strategies, including vaccination. | 1 Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common virus affecting individuals of all ages, the most vulnerable being young children and older adults [1]. RSV can lead to severe infections such as pneumonia in older adults, especially those with chronic cardiovascular disease, pulmonary conditions, or diabetes [1,2,3]. Severe RSV infections may require hospitalization or non-invasive ventilation [1]. RSV is associated with lower and upper respiratory tract disease (LRTD/URTD), potentially leading to inflammatory responses that can cause complications such as exacerbation of asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and heart failure [2]. In Japan, the incidence and disease burden of RSV in older adults is likely underestimated due to the lack of routine testing and surveillance. A prospective study estimated that RSV infection occurs in 2.4% of ambulatory older adults in Japan [4]. A recent meta-analysis using 1999–2020 data from high-income countries estimated approximately 700,000 RSV-related acute respiratory infection (ARI) cases, 63,000 hospitalizations, and 4500 in-hospital deaths annually in older adults in Japan [5]. However, there are currently no specific treatments, highlighting a considerable unmet medical need and the importance of vaccination, especially given the high proportion of Japan’s population that is aged > 65 years (30% in 2022) [11]. papers.title_original: Health and Economic Burden of Severe Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infections Among Older Adults in Japan: A Retrospective Administrative Database Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the health and economic burden of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections in older adults in Japan, as the incidence and disease burden of RSV in this population is likely underestimated due to the lack of routine testing and surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Medical Data Vision (MDV) hospital-based claims database and the insurance-based JMDC database, covering the period from 1 September 2008 to 31 August 2021. The study included 178 cases of RSV infection, with 144 from the MDV database and 34 from the JMDC database, focusing on adults aged ≥ 60 years.
analysis.methods: Data were collected from two anonymized health claims databases, and comparisons were analyzed using a paired sample t-test with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs were compared between pre- and post-event periods.
analysis.main_results: In the MDV cohort, the average number of outpatient visits increased from 1.21 to 2.07, and hospitalizations increased from 0.07 to 0.37 within 30 days post-event, resulting in significant additional medical costs of ¥196,231 (p < 0.001). The impact decreased over time, with no statistical significance detected in the 365-day post-event period. The number of RSV cases increased over the study period, reaching 38 and 36 cases in 2018–2019 and 2019–2020, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the significant health and economic burden of RSV infections in older adults, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions such as vaccination, especially given Japan’s aging population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical insights into the healthcare resource utilization and costs associated with RSV infections in older adults, supporting the development of strategies for surveillance, prevention, and management in this vulnerable group.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on administrative databases, which may lack detailed clinical information. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential for unmeasured confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study examined the health and economic burden of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections in older adults in Japan using data from two health claims databases. The study found that RSV infections led to a significant increase in healthcare resource utilization and medical costs within 30 days of diagnosis, with the impact diminishing over time. These findings underscore the importance of addressing RSV in older populations, particularly given the high proportion of Japan’s aging population. The study's reliance on administrative data limits its depth, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the observational design and potential for confounding factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估日本老年人严重呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染的健康和经济负担,因为由于缺乏常规检测和监测,该人群的RSV发病率和疾病负担可能被低估。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性队列研究研究使用了来自医疗数据愿景(MDV)医院基于的索赔数据库和基于保险的JMDC数据库的数据,时间范围为2008年9月1日至2021年8月31日。研究包括了178例RSV感染病例,其中144例来自MDV数据库,34例来自JMDC数据库,聚焦于≥60岁的成人。
elements_zh.methods: 数据来自两个匿名的健康索赔数据库,使用配对样本t检验进行分析,统计学显著性设定为p < 0.05。比较了医疗资源利用(HCRU)和医疗费用在事件前和事件后期间的变化。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了RSV感染在老年人中的显著健康和经济负担,强调了需要针对性干预措施如疫苗接种,尤其是在日本老龄化人口的背景下。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为了解RSV感染在老年人中的医疗资源利用和费用提供了关键见解,支持针对监测、预防和管理策略的制定,特别是在这一易感人群中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于其依赖行政数据库,可能缺乏详细的临床信息。由于研究的观察性质和潜在的未测量混杂因素,证据强度中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the health and economic burden of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections in older adults in Japan, as the incidence and disease burden of RSV in this population is likely underestimated due to the lack of routine testing and surveillance.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Medical Data Vision (MDV) hospital-based claims database and the insurance-based JMDC database, covering the period from 1 September 2008 to 31 August 2021. The study included 178 cases of RSV infection, with 144 from the MDV database and 34 from the JMDC database, focusing on adults aged ≥ 60 years.
analysis_en.methods: Data were collected from two anonymized health claims databases, and comparisons were analyzed using a paired sample t-test with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs were compared between pre- and post-event periods.
analysis_en.main_results: In the MDV cohort, the average number of outpatient visits increased from 1.21 to 2.07, and hospitalizations increased from 0.07 to 0.37 within 30 days post-event, resulting in significant additional medical costs of ¥196,231 (p < 0.001). The impact decreased over time, with no statistical significance detected in the 365-day post-event period. The number of RSV cases increased over the study period, reaching 38 and 36 cases in 2018–2019 and 2019–2020, respectively.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the significant health and economic burden of RSV infections in older adults, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions such as vaccination, especially given Japan’s aging population.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical insights into the healthcare resource utilization and costs associated with RSV infections in older adults, supporting the development of strategies for surveillance, prevention, and management in this vulnerable group.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on administrative databases, which may lack detailed clinical information. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential for unmeasured confounding factors.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性队列研究研究使用了来自医疗数据愿景(MDV)医院基于的索赔数据库和基于保险的JMDC数据库的数据,时间范围为2008年9月1日至2021年8月31日。研究包括了178例RSV感染病例,其中144例来自MDV数据库,34例来自JMDC数据库,聚焦于≥60岁的成人。
analysis_zh.methods: 数据来自两个匿名的健康索赔数据库,使用配对样本t检验进行分析,统计学显著性设定为p < 0.05。比较了医疗资源利用(HCRU)和医疗费用在事件前和事件后期间的变化。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在MDV 队列研究中,事件后30天内门诊就诊次数平均从1.21次增加到2.07次,住院次数从0.07次增加到0.37次,导致显著增加的医疗费用¥196,231(p < 0.001)。随着时间推移,影响逐渐减弱,在事件后365天期间未检测到统计学显著性。RSV病例数量在研究期间有所增加,分别达到2018–2019年的38例和2019–2020年的36例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了RSV感染在老年人中的显著健康和经济负担,强调了需要针对性干预措施如疫苗接种,尤其是在日本老龄化人口的背景下。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为了解RSV感染在老年人中的医疗资源利用和费用提供了关键见解,支持针对监测、预防和管理策略的制定,特别是在这一易感人群中。

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in children is frequently complicated by bacterial co-infection, which significantly aggravates clinical outcomes. The Albumin-to-Alkaline Phosphatase Ratio (AAPR) has recently emerged as a novel immuno-metabolic marker. This study aimed to investigate the association between AAPR and Gram-positive (G + ) versus Gram-negative (G-) bacterial co-infection phenotypes among RSV-infected children, evaluate its discriminative performance, and explore potentially relevant biological pathways. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 153 pediatric patients with laboratory-confirmed RSV and bacterial co-infection. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were employed to determine the independent association and dose-response relationship between AAPR and infection phenotypes. Diagnostic performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Additionally, an exploratory systems biology analysis was performed to identify candidate genes and signaling pathways potentially relevant to the observed association. Results Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that elevated AAPR was independently and inversely associated with the likelihood of G+ infection (OR = 0.37; 95% CI: 0.15–0.89 for the highest vs. lowest tertile). RCS analysis showed no evidence of a nonlinear association (P for non-linearity = 0.456). The association remained similar after nonlinear adjustment for age and was directionally consistent across age strata; however, it was attenuated after normalization using age-specific pediatric ALP reference limits. AAPR alone showed modest discriminative performance (AUC = 0.599). Addition of AAPR to CRP, WBC, and NEU increased the AUC from 0.455 to 0.613; however, the difference did not reach the conventional threshold for statistical significance (P = 0.051). Exploratory systems biology analysis identified IL-17-, TNF-, and other inflammation-related pathways as candidates for further investigation. Clinical trial number Not applicable. analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in children is frequently complicated by bacterial co-infection, which significantly aggravates clinical outcomes. This study aimed to investigate the association between AAPR and Gram-positive (G + ) versus Gram-negative (G-) bacterial co-infection phenotypes among RSV-infected children, evaluate its discriminative performance, and explore potentially relevant biological pathways.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We retrospectively analyzed 153 pediatric patients with laboratory-confirmed RSV and bacterial co-infection. The study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Second Affiliated Hospital and Yuying Children’s Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University.
analysis.methods: Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were employed to determine the independent association and dose-response relationship between AAPR and infection phenotypes. Diagnostic performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). An exploratory systems biology analysis was performed to identify candidate genes and signaling pathways potentially relevant to the observed association.
analysis.main_results: Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that elevated AAPR was independently and inversely associated with the likelihood of G+ infection (OR = 0.37; 95% CI: 0.15–0.89 for the highest vs. RCS analysis showed no evidence of a nonlinear association (P for non-linearity = 0.456). AAPR alone showed modest discriminative performance (AUC = 0.599). Addition of AAPR to CRP, WBC, and NEU increased the AUC from 0.455 to 0.613; however, the difference did not reach the conventional threshold for statistical significance (P = 0.051).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The Albumin-to-Alkaline Phosphatase Ratio (AAPR) has recently emerged as a novel immuno-metabolic marker. Exploratory systems biology analysis identified IL-17-, TNF-, and other inflammation-related pathways as candidates for further investigation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of immuno-metabolic markers for early detection of bacterial co-infection in RSV-infected children. These insights could contribute to improved diagnostic strategies and targeted therapeutic approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The association was attenuated after normalization using age-specific pediatric ALP reference limits, and the difference in AUC did not reach the conventional threshold for statistical significance. The study is retrospective and based on de-identified clinical data, which may introduce bias and limit generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between the Albumin-to-Alkaline Phosphatase Ratio (AAPR) and bacterial co-infection phenotypes in children with Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infection. The research highlights the potential of AAPR as an immuno-metabolic marker for distinguishing Gram-positive from Gram-negative bacterial co-infections. Results show an inverse association between elevated AAPR and G+ infection, though this was attenuated after normalization. AAPR demonstrated modest discriminative performance, and its addition to standard markers like CRP, WBC, and NEU slightly improved diagnostic accuracy without reaching statistical significance. The study also identified inflammation-related pathways as candidates for further investigation. However, limitations include the retrospective design and potential bias from de-identified data, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate in strength, with findings grounded in statistical analysis and systems biology approaches.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 儿童 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染经常并发细菌合并感染,这会显着恶化临床结果。本研究旨在调查 RSV 感染儿童中 AAPR 与革兰氏阳性 (G + ) 和革兰氏阴性 (G-) 细菌共感染表型之间的关联,评估其区分性能,并探索潜在的相关生物学途径。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们回顾性分析了 153 名实验室确诊的 RSV 和细菌合并感染的儿童患者。该研究按照赫尔辛基宣言进行,并获得温州医科大学第二附属医院和育英儿童医院伦理委员会批准。
elements_zh.methods: 采用多变量逻辑回归和限制三次样条 (RCS) 分析来确定 AAPR 和感染表型之间的独立关联和剂量反应关系。使用受试者工作特征曲线下面积(AUC)对诊断性能进行量化。进行了探索性系统生物学分析,以确定与观察到的关联可能相关的候选基因和信号通路。
elements_zh.main_results: 多变量逻辑回归表明,升高的 AAPR 与 G+ 感染的可能性独立且呈负相关(OR = 0.37;95% CI:0.15-0.89,最高与 RCS 分析显示没有非线性关联的证据(非线性 P = 0.456)。单独的 AAPR 显示出适度的判别性能(AUC = 0.599)。将 AAPR 添加到 CRP、WBC、 NEU 将 AUC 从 0.455 增加到 0.613;然而,差异并未达到统计学显着性的常规阈值(P = 0.051)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 白蛋白与碱性磷酸酶比率(AAPR)最近成为一种新型免疫代谢标志物。探索性系统生物学分析确定了 IL-17、TNF 和其他炎症相关途径作为进一步研究的候选途径。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发免疫代谢标记物,以早期检测 RSV 感染儿童的细菌合并感染。这些见解可能有助于改进诊断策略和有针对性的治疗方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 使用特定年龄的儿科 ALP 参考限进行标准化后,这种关联性减弱,并且 AUC 的差异未达到统计显着性的常规阈值。该研究是回顾性的,基于未识别的临床数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制普遍性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 儿童 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染经常并发细菌合并感染,这会显着恶化临床结果。本研究旨在调查 RSV 感染儿童中 AAPR 与革兰氏阳性 (G + ) 和革兰氏阴性 (G-) 细菌共感染表型之间的关联,评估其区分性能,并探索潜在的相关生物学途径。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们回顾性分析了 153 名实验室确诊的 RSV 和细菌合并感染的儿童患者。该研究按照赫尔辛基宣言进行,并获得温州医科大学第二附属医院和育英儿童医院伦理委员会批准。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用多变量逻辑回归和限制三次样条 (RCS) 分析来确定 AAPR 和感染表型之间的独立关联和剂量反应关系。使用受试者工作特征曲线下面积(AUC)对诊断性能进行量化。进行了探索性系统生物学分析,以确定与观察到的关联可能相关的候选基因和信号通路。
analysis_zh.main_results: 多变量逻辑回归表明,升高的 AAPR 与 G+ 感染的可能性独立且呈负相关(OR = 0.37;95% CI:0.15-0.89,最高与 RCS 分析显示没有非线性关联的证据(非线性 P = 0.456)。单独的 AAPR 显示出适度的判别性能(AUC = 0.599)。将 AAPR 添加到 CRP、WBC、 NEU 将 AUC 从 0.455 增加到 0.613;然而,差异并未达到统计学显着性的常规阈值(P = 0.051)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 白蛋白与碱性磷酸酶比率(AAPR)最近成为一种新型免疫代谢标志物。探索性系统生物学分析确定了 IL-17、TNF 和其他炎症相关途径作为进一步研究的候选途径。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发免疫代谢标记物,以早期检测 RSV 感染儿童的细菌合并感染。这些见解可能有助于改进诊断策略和有针对性的治疗方法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 使用特定年龄的儿科 ALP 参考限进行标准化后,这种关联性减弱,并且 AUC 的差异未达到统计显着性的常规阈值。该研究是回顾性的,基于未识别的临床数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制普遍性。

papers.title: RSV: A Training-Free Verification Framework for Proactive and Efficient Online Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Online video understanding requires models to proactively decide when to respond and which information to preserve from inherently redundant continuous visual streams. However, current online Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) either operate in a reactive, query-driven manner with limited autonomy, or rely on active mechanisms that demand costly instruction tuning yet still yield suboptimal performance. Moreover, these existing paradigms often face challenges in effectively reducing the dense spatiotemporal redundancy of continuous video streams. To address these limitations, we propose Reference State Verification (RSV), a generalized, training-free paradigm that transforms pre-trained offline Video-LLMs into proactive online assistants through semantic state comparison. Building upon RSV, we first introduce Attention Distribution Divergence (ADD), utilizing the relative deviation of cross-modal attention as a robust verification signal for autonomous response triggering. Furthermore, we present Verification-guided Spatio-Temporal Compression (VSTC), which re-purposes these verification signals as a free byproduct to achieve multi-granular redundancy elimination, including semantic-guided frame dropping and fine-grained spatial token pruning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our plug-and-play approach significantly enhances the inference efficiency and proactive responsiveness of various Video-LLMs without requiring any architectural modifications or parameter fine-tuning.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究引入了一种名为参考状态验证(RSV)的免培训框架,将预先训练的离线视频法学硕士转变为主动的在线助手,重点关注管理连续视觉数据流的挑战。
elements_zh.methods: 该框架利用语义状态比较来实现主动决策,并引入注意力分布分歧(ADD)作为基于跨模式注意力偏差的验证信号。此外,验证引导的时空压缩 (VSTC) 通过语义引导的帧丢弃和空间令牌修剪重新调整这些信号的用途,以消除冗余。
elements_zh.main_results: 大量实验表明,即插即用方法显着提高了各种 Video-LLM 的推理效率和主动响应能力,而无需更改架构或参数微调。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更高效、更自主的视频理解系统提供信息,该系统可能应用于公共卫生和科学研究的视频内容的实时监控和分析。

papers.title_zh: RSV:一种无需培训的验证框架,可实现主动高效的在线视频理解
papers.source_body_en: Online video understanding requires models to proactively decide when to respond and which information to preserve from inherently redundant continuous visual streams. However, current online Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) either operate in a reactive, query-driven manner with limited autonomy, or rely on active mechanisms that demand costly instruction tuning yet still yield suboptimal performance. Moreover, these existing paradigms often face challenges in effectively reducing the dense spatiotemporal redundancy of continuous video streams. To address these limitations, we propose Reference State Verification (RSV), a generalized, training-free paradigm that transforms pre-trained offline Video-LLMs into proactive online assistants through semantic state comparison. Building upon RSV, we first introduce Attention Distribution Divergence (ADD), utilizing the relative deviation of cross-modal attention as a robust verification signal for autonomous response triggering. Furthermore, we present Verification-guided Spatio-Temporal Compression (VSTC), which re-purposes these verification signals as a free byproduct to achieve multi-granular redundancy elimination, including semantic-guided frame dropping and fine-grained spatial token pruning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our plug-and-play approach significantly enhances the inference efficiency and proactive responsiveness of various Video-LLMs without requiring any architectural modifications or parameter fine-tuning.
papers.abstract_zh: 在线视频理解需要模型主动决定何时响应以及从固有冗余的连续视觉流中保留哪些信息。然而,当前的在线视频大语言模型(Video-LLM)要么以反应式、查询驱动的方式运行,自主性有限,要么依赖主动机制,需要昂贵的指令调整,但仍然产生次优性能。此外,这些现有的范例在有效减少连续视频流的密集时空冗余方面常常面临挑战。为了解决这些限制,我们提出了参考状态验证(RSV),这是一种通用的、免训练的范式,可通过语义状态比较将预先训练的离线视频法学硕士转变为主动的在线助手。在 RSV 的基础上,我们首先引入注意力分布散度(ADD),利用跨模态注意力的相对偏差作为自主响应触发的鲁棒验证信号。此外,我们提出了验证引导的时空压缩(VSTC),它将这些验证信号重新用作免费的副产品,以实现多粒度的冗余消除,包括语义引导的帧丢弃和细粒度的空间令牌修剪。大量实验表明,我们的即插即用方法显着提高了各种视频法学硕士的推理效率和主动响应能力,无需任何架构修改或参数微调。

papers.title: Clinically relevant RSV anti-F antibodies exhibit comparable inhibition of syncytium formation despite marked differences in neutralization potency
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants, immunocompromised individuals, and older adults. A hallmark of RSV infection is the formation of multinucleated syncytia through fusion between infected and adjacent uninfected cells. This process is mediated by the RSV fusion protein (RSV F) expressed on infected cells, which interacts with receptors on neighboring cells to drive membrane fusion. Syncytium formation may facilitate cell-to-cell spread while reducing virion exposure to extracellular neutralizing antibodies and immune cells. Clinically used monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) target RSV F and are routinely evaluated using conventional virus neutralization assays. However, their ability to inhibit syncytium formation remains poorly characterized because these assays primarily measure virus-to-cell entry rather than cell-to-cell fusion. Here, we present a quantitative flow cytometry-based assay to measure RSV-induced syncytium formation during infection. Using this assay, we evaluated clinically relevant anti-F mAbs and compared their potency in syncytium inhibition and conventional virus neutralization assays in HEp-2 and A549 cells. Palivizumab, nirsevimab, and clesrovimab inhibited syncytium formation in a dose-dependent manner, with only modest differences in potency. In contrast, nirsevimab and clesrovimab exhibited substantially greater virus neutralization potency than palivizumab. These findings indicate that inhibition of RSV-induced cell-to-cell fusion represents a distinct functional property of anti-F antibodies that is not fully captured by conventional neutralization assays. Our assay provides a quantitative approach to assess syncytium inhibition and highlights the value of complementary functional readouts for evaluating antibodies targeting RSV and other syncytium-forming viruses. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory disease in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. A hallmark of RSV infection is syncytium formation, although its contribution to viral spread and disease pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Increased fusogenicity has been associated with disease severity, and syncytium formation may promote cell-to-cell spread while limiting virion exposure to extracellular neutralizing antibodies. Although RSV fusion (F)-specific monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are increasingly used for disease prevention, their ability to inhibit syncytium formation remains unexplored, as conventional neutralization assays primarily measure virus-to-cell entry. Here, we describe a quantitative flow cytometry-based assay to measure RSV-induced syncytium formation and evaluate inhibition by clinically relevant anti-F mAbs. Our results indicate that syncytium inhibition represents a distinct functional property of anti-F antibodies that is not fully captured by conventional neutralization assays, highlighting the value of complementary functional readouts for evaluating antibodies targeting RSV and other syncytium-forming viruses.

Here, we describe a quantitative flow cytometry-based assay to measure RSV-induced syncytium formation and evaluate inhibition by clinically relevant anti-F mAbs. Our results indicate that syncytium inhibition represents a distinct functional property of anti-F antibodies that is not fully captured by conventional neutralization assays, highlighting the value of complementary functional readouts for evaluating antibodies targeting RSV and other syncytium-forming viruses.

papers.title: Public Health Impact of Universal Nirsevimab Prophylaxis: A Multicenter Study on the Reduction of RSV Hospitalizations in Infants in Tuscany, Italy.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nirsevimab is a long-acting monoclonal antibody approved for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in infants. Although growing real-world evidence supports its effectiveness, large multicenter studies assessing the population-level impact of universal immunization remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study involving nearly the entire pediatric hospital network in Tuscany, Italy. The public health impact of the universal nirsevimab program was assessed through a pre-post comparison of the 2023-24 and 2024-25 RSV seasons. We evaluated RSV-related hospitalizations, respiratory support requirements and healthcare resource utilization. Nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalization was estimated using the screening method. FINDINGS: RSV-related hospitalizations declined from 533 cases in 2023-24 to 104 in 2024-25, corresponding to an 80.5% reduction (IRR 0.20, 95% CI 0.16-0.24; p<0.001). Significant reductions were observed across all markers of disease severity, respiratory support requirements and healthcare utilization, including PICU admissions (-87.0%), low-flow oxygen therapy (-78.7%), high-flow oxygen therapy (-81.0%), non-invasive ventilation (-85.0%), bronchodilator use (-82.3%), corticosteroid use (-89.3%), and antibiotic therapy (-84.5%). Infants born outside the RSV season accounted for a substantial proportion of RSV-related hospitalizations and severe disease during the pre-intervention season. Estimated effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalization was 89.7% (95% CI 85.4-92.7%). A limited number of breakthrough hospitalizations were observed throughout the RSV season without an accumulation towards the end of RSV season, Although these findings do not constitute a formal evaluation of durability of protection, they suggest that protection does not show a substantial decline over the RSV season. INTERPRETATION: Universal nirsevimab immunization was associated with substantial reductions in RSV-related hospitalizations, disease severity, and healthcare resource utilization across Tuscany. This large multicenter study demonstrates a major population-level impact and high real-world effectiveness. Breakthrough hospitalizations occurred throughout the RSV season and did not show a progressive increase across longer post-administration intervals, although the available data do not allow a formal assessment of waning protection. The findings also underscore the important contribution of infants born outside the traditional RSV season to the overall RSV burden, supporting prevention strategies that protect the entire birth cohort.

papers.title: Transplacental transfer efficiency and longitudinal dynamics of antibodies against RSV in early childhood: a paired mother-neonate cohort study in southern China.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Maternal antibodies provide early-life protection against severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection but wane rapidly. With the availability of maternal vaccine and half-life extended monoclonal antibodies for infants, understanding transplacental antibody transfer and subsequent antibody dynamics is important for optimising immunisation strategies. METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal cohort study of 695 mother-neonate pairs in southern China between 2013 and 2021. Serum samples were collected from mothers at delivery and from children at birth, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, 36 months, and 5-8 years of age. All samples were tested for RSV pre-F IgG antibodies using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. A subset of samples was additionally tested for neutralizing antibodies (nAbs) using a foci reduction neutralization test. RESULTS: Maternal and cord blood RSV pre-F IgG antibody levels were positively correlated ( = 0.87; P<0.001) with a mean transplacental transfer ratio of 1.44 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.40-1.47). A 10-fold increase in maternal antibody levels was associated with a 6.46-fold increase in cord blood antibody levels, corresponding to a 35% decrease in transplacental transfer ratios. Preterm birth was associated with 17% lower cord blood antibody levels than full-term birth. Maternally derived antibodies declined rapidly after birth, with an estimated half-life of 34.3 days (95% CI, 33.9-34.8); antibody levels reached a nadir at approximately 10 months of age and gradually increased thereafter. RSV pre-F IgG and nAb titers from children were strongly correlated (repeated-measures correlation: = 0.846, P < 0.001), and the correlation persisted after adjustment for age ( = 0.743, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the importance of addressing lower maternally derived antibody levels in preterm infants, particularly in the context of maternal immunisation. Longitudinal antibody dynamics reveal a distinct period of low antibody levels during infancy that may inform the timing of targeted RSV immunisation strategies.

papers.title: Epidemiology of acute respiratory infections in adult patients in Hospices Civils de Lyon, France, between October 2016 and April 2025
papers.abstract: Background Multiple viruses can cause acute respiratory infections (ARI), impacting morbidity, mortality and hospital resources. The objective of this study was to describe viral circulation among patients with ARI, patients characteristics and severity outcomes. Methods A retrospective cohort was assembled using electronic health records from the Hospices Civils de Lyon, France. Adult patients ([≥]18 years) hospitalised or presenting to the emergency department from October 2016 to April 2025 with either an ICD-10 diagnostic code for ARI or a laboratory-confirmed viral detection were included. Administrative variables and laboratory results collected during the stay were extracted. Results 103,011 hospital visits involving 82,077 patients were included. The number of eligible stays increased substantially since the COVID-19 pandemic, along with year-round laboratory testing. Following disruption during the pandemic, winter peaks of ARI incidence, influenza and RSV detections re-emerged after 2022. Influenza, rhinovirus and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates peaked in younger adults (<65 years), whereas RSV and hMPV positivity rates were highest in patients aged [≥]80 years. Patients aged [≥]65 years had longer hospitalisations (median 10 vs 8 days, p<0.001), twice in-hospital mortality rate (14% vs 7%, p<0.001), less frequent ICU admission (21% vs 33%, p<0.001) and use of respiratory support than younger adults. Influenza was the virus associated with the shortest length of stays, hMPV was associated with the longest in younger adults. Conclusions Real-world hospital data are valuable for surveillance of viral circulation, early identification of patients at risk of deterioration, and may be used to evaluate the impact of preventive intervention in community.
authors: Marta Cristina dos Santos Bispo Nunes

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to describe viral circulation among adult patients with acute respiratory infections (ARI) in France, addressing the need to understand the impact of multiple viruses on morbidity, mortality, and hospital resources.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using electronic health records from the Hospices Civils de Lyon, France, involving adult patients (≥18 years) hospitalised or presenting to the emergency department from October 2016 to April 2025 with either an ICD-10 diagnostic code for ARI or a laboratory-confirmed viral detection.
analysis.methods: Methods included the assembly of a retrospective cohort using electronic health records, extraction of administrative variables and laboratory results during the hospital stay, and analysis of data from October 2016 to April 2025.
analysis.main_results: The study included 103,011 hospital visits involving 82,077 patients, with a substantial increase in eligible stays since the COVID-19 pandemic, along with year-round laboratory testing. Winter peaks of ARI incidence, influenza, and RSV detections re-emerged after 2022.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that influenza, rhinovirus, and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates peaked in younger adults (<65 years), whereas RSV and hMPV positivity rates were highest in patients aged ≥80 years. Patients aged ≥65 years had longer hospitalisations, higher mortality rates, and less frequent ICU admission and respiratory support compared to younger adults.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance of viral circulation, early identification of patients at risk of deterioration, and evaluation of the impact of preventive interventions in the community.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, potential for bias in data collection, and the lack of specific RSV data, which may affect the generalisability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study described the viral circulation among adult patients with acute respiratory infections in France, highlighting the impact of various viruses on patient outcomes and hospital resources. The findings can inform surveillance and preventive interventions.

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using electronic health records from the Hospices Civils de Lyon, France, involving adult patients (≥18 years) hospitalised or presenting to the emergency department from October 2016 to April 2025 with either an ICD-10 diagnostic code for ARI or a laboratory-confirmed viral detection.
analysis_en.methods: Methods included the assembly of a retrospective cohort using electronic health records, extraction of administrative variables and laboratory results during the hospital stay, and analysis of data from October 2016 to April 2025.
analysis_en.main_results: The study included 103,011 hospital visits involving 82,077 patients, with a substantial increase in eligible stays since the COVID-19 pandemic, along with year-round laboratory testing. Winter peaks of ARI incidence, influenza, and RSV detections re-emerged after 2022.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that influenza, rhinovirus, and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates peaked in younger adults (<65 years), whereas RSV and hMPV positivity rates were highest in patients aged ≥80 years. Patients aged ≥65 years had longer hospitalisations, higher mortality rates, and less frequent ICU admission and respiratory support compared to younger adults.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance of viral circulation, early identification of patients at risk of deterioration, and evaluation of the impact of preventive interventions in the community.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, potential for bias in data collection, and the lack of specific RSV data, which may affect the generalisability of the findings.

papers.title_zh: 法国里昂民事医院成人急性呼吸道感染患者2016年10月至2025年4月期间的病毒流行情况
papers.source_body_en: Background Multiple viruses can cause acute respiratory infections (ARI), impacting morbidity, mortality and hospital resources. The objective of this study was to describe viral circulation among patients with ARI, patients characteristics and severity outcomes. Methods A retrospective cohort was assembled using electronic health records from the Hospices Civils de Lyon, France. Adult patients ([≥]18 years) hospitalised or presenting to the emergency department from October 2016 to April 2025 with either an ICD-10 diagnostic code for ARI or a laboratory-confirmed viral detection were included. Administrative variables and laboratory results collected during the stay were extracted. Results 103,011 hospital visits involving 82,077 patients were included. The number of eligible stays increased substantially since the COVID-19 pandemic, along with year-round laboratory testing. Following disruption during the pandemic, winter peaks of ARI incidence, influenza and RSV detections re-emerged after 2022. Influenza, rhinovirus and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates peaked in younger adults (<65 years), whereas RSV and hMPV positivity rates were highest in patients aged [≥]80 years. Patients aged [≥]65 years had longer hospitalisations (median 10 vs 8 days, p<0.001), twice in-hospital mortality rate (14% vs 7%, p<0.001), less frequent ICU admission (21% vs 33%, p<0.001) and use of respiratory support than younger adults. Influenza was the virus associated with the shortest length of stays, hMPV was associated with the longest in younger adults. Conclusions Real-world hospital data are valuable for surveillance of viral circulation, early identification of patients at risk of deterioration, and may be used to evaluate the impact of preventive intervention in community.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在描述法国里昂民事医院成人急性呼吸道感染(ARI)患者中的病毒流行情况,以满足对多种病毒对发病率、死亡率和医院资源影响的理解需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用法国里昂民事医院的电子健康记录,回顾性地整理了相关数据,纳入了2016年10月至2025年4月期间年龄≥18岁的成人患者,其住院或急诊就诊时具有ARI的ICD-10诊断代码或实验室确认的病毒检测结果。
analysis_zh.methods: 方法包括回顾性整理电子健康记录、提取住院期间的行政变量和实验室结果,并分析2016年10月至2025年4月期间的数据。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,流感、鼻病毒和SARS-CoV-2的阳性率在年轻成人(<65岁)中达到峰值,而RSV和hMPV的阳性率在年龄≥80岁的患者中最高。年龄≥65岁的患者住院时间更长,住院死亡率更高,但较少需要ICU入住和呼吸支持,与年轻成人相比。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可用于病毒流行监测、早期识别可能恶化的患者,以及评估社区预防干预的影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计,数据收集可能存在偏倚,且缺乏特定的RSV数据,这可能影响研究结果的普遍适用性。

papers.title: Viral Aetiology of Lower Respiratory Tract Infections in Infants Attending Primary Care in Eastern Spain, 2023-2025.
papers.abstract: To describe seasonal patterns of respiratory viruses in infants presenting to primary care (PC) after the rollout of the RSV-immunisation programme in Spain, we analysed multiplex RT-PCR results from infants <1 year with lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) attending 57 PC centres in Valencia and Murcia across two seasons. Among the 307 infants, rhinovirus/enterovirus and RSV were the most common detections in both periods. hMPV, bocavirus, and influenza followed. Our findings highlight the importance of community-based surveillance systems for providing real-world evidence to inform future immunisation strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the seasonal patterns of respiratory viruses in infants under one year of age attending primary care centres in Valencia and Murcia, Spain, following the rollout of an RSV-immunisation programme. Multiplex RT-PCR was used to detect viral aetiology in 307 infants with lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) over two seasons. The most common detections were rhinovirus/enterovirus and RSV, with hMPV, bocavirus, and influenza also identified. The findings highlight the importance of community-based surveillance systems in providing real-world evidence to inform future immunisation strategies. The study's limitations include its focus on two seasons and primary care settings, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational design and the absence of control groups.

papers.title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Antimicrobial Resistance Profiles of Haemophilus influenzae Respiratory Infections in Hospitalized Children: A 7-Year Retrospective Study in Kunming
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective To analyze age, sex, temporal patterns, co-detected pathogens and sputum-culture antimicrobial resistance of Haemophilus influenzae (Hi) respiratory infections among hospitalized children in Kunming from 2019 to 2025, so as to provide evidence for local prevention, control and rational selection of antimicrobial agents. Methods This retrospective study included hospitalized children diagnosed with Hi respiratory tract infection. We stratified and summarized epidemiological characteristics, co-infecting pathogens and antimicrobial susceptibility results of sputum isolates according to age group, month, season and gender. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 分析2019年至2025年间昆明市住院儿童流感嗜血杆菌(Hi)呼吸道感染的年龄、性别、时间分布模式、共感染病原体及痰培养抗菌药物耐药情况,以提供本地预防、控制和抗菌药物合理选择的依据。方法 本回顾性研究纳入了被诊断为流感嗜血杆菌呼吸道感染的住院儿童。根据年龄组、月份、季节和性别对流行病学特征、共感染病原体及抗菌药物敏感性结果进行分层总结。结果 共确认11,217例病例,通过痰培养或PCR检测。年病例数波动增加,2020年达到最低水平,2024-2025年达到最高水平,冬季和春季有明显聚集趋势。学龄前及学龄儿童的比例逐渐上升,而婴儿的比例显著下降(P < 0.001)。尽管男孩仍占主导地位,但女孩的比例逐年上升。常见的共感染病原体包括肺炎链球菌、呼吸道合胞病毒、副流感病毒、鼻病毒、腺病毒和肺炎支原体,且共感染模式在不同年份、季节和年龄组间差异显著。氨苄西林、复方新诺明和头孢氯苄表现出较高的耐药性,而头孢曲松、头孢噻肟、利福平、美罗培南和喹诺酮类药物保持良好的抗菌活性。结论 儿童流感嗜血杆菌呼吸道感染呈现冬春双峰流行趋势,并且年龄分布向较大儿童转移。建议将第三代头孢菌素作为经验性治疗的一线药物。持续的本地监测和耐药性数据应指导临床抗生素的使用。

papers.title: An Interferon-Braked Monocyte State and Compartment-Specific Myeloid Programming Across Severe Respiratory Infections
papers.abstract: Severe COVID-19 is accompanied by marked remodeling of airway myeloid compartments, yet how infiltrating monocytes are routed toward inflammatory versus pro-fibrotic fates, and why resident alveolar macrophages fail to recover, remains incompletely understood. We re-analyzed BALF single-cell data (GSE145926; 3 healthy, 3 mild/moderate, 6 severe; 27,807 cells), re-clustering myeloid cells (n = 19,485) into 37 fine states (13 families) with functional module scoring, diffusion pseudotime, PAGA, a curated ligand–receptor screen, and per-donor decomposition; validation used the independent fatal-COVID-19 BALF cohort GSE157344 and the healthy-BALF cohort GSE151928 as a specificity control, a human endotoxin bone-marrow comparator (GSE212092), two sepsis blood cohorts (GSE175453; GSE167363, paired 0 h/6 h), three cross-pathogen blood cohorts (influenza A GSE243629, infant RSV GSE283746, bacterial ARDS GSE157789), and cross-disease comparison with IPF lung (GSE128033). Healthy BALF comprised resident alveolar macrophages, depleted in severe disease and replaced by interferon-activated, CXCL8-high, and SPP1+ populations. A CD14+SPP1−FCN1+ population co-expressing interferon-stimulated genes and IL1RN—an interferon-braked state distinct from LPS-type trained immunity—was enriched in severe disease, driven predominantly by one patient. PAGA delineated an FCN1+→intermediate→SPP1+ continuum; severe-enriched circuits included MIF–CD74 and an autocrine CXCL8–CXCR2 loop. The interferon-braked signature and SPP1+ compartments were reproduced in an independent fatal-COVID-19 BALF cohort and were at baseline in a healthy-BALF reference cohort (0.343 ± 0.091); LPS-challenged marrow showed the reciprocal pattern (TLR4-high, interferon-silent); and IPF lung shared SPP1/TREM2 induction with resident-AM collapse (SPP1 p = 0.0005). In sepsis blood, monocytes retained the interferon-braked signature with the LPS/TLR4 module near baseline; the signature was likewise elevated in bacterial ARDS, influenza A, and infant RSV monocytes, extending the compartment model beyond COVID-19. The data support a two-signal model: interferon restrains recruited monocytes at entry, while TLR4/HIF-1α- and SPP1-associated programs act downstream. The brake state is a measurable, stage-specific marker; MIF–CD74, CXCL8–CXCR2, and SPP1–CD44 are candidate nodes for stage-specific intervention. These mechanistic interpretations are grounded in the data and are proposed as testable hypotheses.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Severe COVID-19 is accompanied by marked remodeling of airway myeloid compartments, yet how infiltrating monocytes are routed toward inflammatory versus pro-fibrotic fates, and why resident alveolar macrophages fail to recover, remains incompletely understood.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: We re-analyzed BALF single-cell data (GSE145926; 3 healthy, 3 mild/moderate, 6 severe; 27,807 cells), re-clustering myeloid cells (n = 19,485) into 37 fine states (13 families) with functional module scoring, diffusion pseudotime, PAGA, a curated ligand–receptor screen, and per-donor decomposition; validation used the independent fatal-COVID-19 BALF cohort GSE157344 and the healthy-BALF cohort GSE151928 as a specificity control, a human endotoxin bone-marrow comparator (GSE212092), two sepsis blood cohorts (GSE175453; GSE167363, paired 0 h/6 h), three cross-pathogen blood cohorts (influenza A GSE243629, infant RSV GSE283746, bacterial ARDS GSE157789), and cross-disease comparison with IPF lung (GSE128033).
elements_en.methods: Healthy BALF comprised resident alveolar macrophages, depleted in severe disease and replaced by interferon-activated, CXCL8-high, and SPP1+ populations. A CD14+SPP1−FCN1+ population co-expressing interferon-stimulated genes and IL1RN—an interferon-braked state distinct from LPS-type trained immunity—was enriched in severe disease, driven predominantly by one patient. PAGA delineated an FCN1+→intermediate→SPP1+ continuum; severe-enriched circuits included MIF–CD74 and an autocrine CXCL8–CXCR2 loop.
elements_en.main_results: The interferon-braked signature and SPP1+ compartments were reproduced in an independent fatal-COVID-19 BALF cohort and were at baseline in a healthy-BALF reference cohort (0.343 ± 0.091); LPS-challenged marrow showed the reciprocal pattern (TLR4-high, interferon-silent); and IPF lung shared SPP1/TREM2 induction with resident-AM collapse (SPP1 p = 0.0005). elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The data support a two-signal model: interferon restrains recruited monocytes at entry, while TLR4/HIF-1α- and SPP1-associated programs act downstream. The brake state is a measurable, stage-specific marker; MIF–CD74, CXCL8–CXCR2, and SPP1–CD44 are candidate nodes for stage-specific intervention. These mechanistic interpretations are grounded in the data and are proposed as testable hypotheses.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment of severe respiratory infections, including COVID-19, by identifying a measurable, stage-specific marker for interferon-braked monocytes. This could aid in understanding and managing the progression of severe respiratory diseases.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of single-cell data from BALF, which may not fully capture systemic responses. The findings are specific to the context of severe respiratory infections and may not generalize to other diseases or settings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the need for further validation in larger, more diverse cohorts.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于使用来自BALF的单细胞数据,这可能无法充分反映全身性反应。研究结果特指严重呼吸道感染的背景,可能无法推广至其他疾病或情境。由于研究具有观察性质,证据强度中等,需要在更大、更具多样性的队列研究中进一步验证。

papers.title: Dual-aptamer magnetic capture and electrochemical detection of influenza B and respiratory syncytial viruses in artificial saliva.
papers.abstract: Saliva is a promising non-invasive specimen for respiratory virus diagnostics but its biochemical complexity challenges direct interfacing with affinity-based biosensors. We report a dual-aptamer magnetic-capture electrochemical assay for detection of influenza B virus (IBV) and human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) in artificial saliva. For each target virus, two sequence-distinct DNA aptamers are used: an amino-modified capture aptamer (IBV1 or RSV1) covalently coupled to ∼5 μm polydopamine-coated magnetic microparticles by direct Schiff-base reaction with the polydopamine quinone/catechol surface, and a thiol-modified detection aptamer (IBV2 or RSV2) self-assembled on screen-printed gold electrodes via thiol-gold chemistry. After a single multiplexed batch capture step with both aptamer-magnetic-particle types, the pellet is split and analysed in parallel on the two aptamer-modified electrodes by square-wave voltammetry (SWV). Langmuir analysis of the SWV calibration curves yielded apparent dissociation constants of Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1 (IBV) and 226 ± 85 PFU mL-1 (hRSV), with detection limits of 15 and 11 PFU mL-1, respectively. Log-linear calibration spanned 101-104 PFU mL-1 on both channels (n = 4 concentrations, R2 = 0.995 and 0.990) with sensitivities of 8.58 and 6.61 μA per decade, so that each virus-specific assay covers three orders of magnitude of viral load. The sequence-orthogonal dual-aptamer geometry-capture and detection recognitions targeting non-identical epitopes-is proposed as the structural mitigation. This proof-of-concept establishes a programmable, saliva-compatible architecture reconfigurable for emerging respiratory pathogens by aptamer substitution alone.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a dual-aptamer magnetic capture and electrochemical detection method for identifying influenza B virus (IBV) and human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) in artificial saliva. The approach uses sequence-distinct DNA aptamers for capture and detection, with the capture aptamer attached to magnetic microparticles and the detection aptamer on gold electrodes. The method enables parallel analysis of both viruses after a single capture step. The results show apparent dissociation constants of Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1 for IBV and 226 ± 85 PFU mL-1 for hRSV, with detection limits of 15 and 11 PFU mL-1, respectively. The authors propose this method as a structural mitigation strategy for non-invasive virus detection, highlighting its potential for reconfiguration to detect emerging respiratory pathogens. The study is a proof-of-concept and does not address limitations or evidence strength directly.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 唾液是一种有前景的非侵入性样本,用于呼吸道病毒的诊断,但其生化复杂性对直接与基于亲和力的生物传感器进行接口提出了挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们报告了一种双适配体磁捕获电化学检测方法,用于在人工唾液中检测流感B病毒(IBV)和人类呼吸道合胞病毒(hRSV)
elements_zh.methods: 对于每种目标病毒,使用两种序列不同的DNA适配体:一种是氨基修饰的捕获适配体(IBV1或RSV1),通过直接席夫碱反应与约5微米聚多巴胺包被的磁性微粒共价偶联;另一种是硫醇修饰的检测适配体(IBV2或RSV2),通过硫醇-金化学自组装于丝网印刷金电极上。
elements_zh.main_results: 在单次多路复用批量捕获步骤后,使用两种适配体-磁性微粒类型捕获样本,然后将沉淀物分成两部分,分别在两种适配体修饰的电极上通过方波伏安法(SWV)进行并行分析。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 对SWV校准曲线进行朗缪尔分析,得到的表观解离常数为Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1(IBV)和226 ± 85 PFU mL-1(hRSV),检测限分别为15和11 PFU mL-1。

papers.title_zh: 双适体磁性捕获和电化学检测人工唾液中的 B 型流感病毒和 呼吸道合胞病毒。
papers.source_body_en: Saliva is a promising non-invasive specimen for respiratory virus diagnostics but its biochemical complexity challenges direct interfacing with affinity-based biosensors. We report a dual-aptamer magnetic-capture electrochemical assay for detection of influenza B virus (IBV) and human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) in artificial saliva. For each target virus, two sequence-distinct DNA aptamers are used: an amino-modified capture aptamer (IBV1 or RSV1) covalently coupled to ∼5 μm polydopamine-coated magnetic microparticles by direct Schiff-base reaction with the polydopamine quinone/catechol surface, and a thiol-modified detection aptamer (IBV2 or RSV2) self-assembled on screen-printed gold electrodes via thiol-gold chemistry. After a single multiplexed batch capture step with both aptamer-magnetic-particle types, the pellet is split and analysed in parallel on the two aptamer-modified electrodes by square-wave voltammetry (SWV). Langmuir analysis of the SWV calibration curves yielded apparent dissociation constants of Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1 (IBV) and 226 ± 85 PFU mL-1 (hRSV), with detection limits of 15 and 11 PFU mL-1, respectively. Log-linear calibration spanned 101-104 PFU mL-1 on both channels (n = 4 concentrations, R2 = 0.995 and 0.990) with sensitivities of 8.58 and 6.61 μA per decade, so that each virus-specific assay covers three orders of magnitude of viral load. The sequence-orthogonal dual-aptamer geometry-capture and detection recognitions targeting non-identical epitopes-is proposed as the structural mitigation. This proof-of-concept establishes a programmable, saliva-compatible architecture reconfigurable for emerging respiratory pathogens by aptamer substitution alone.
papers.abstract_zh: 唾液是一种很有前途的呼吸道病毒诊断非侵入性样本,但其生化复杂性挑战了与基于亲和力的生物传感器的直接连接。我们报告了一种双适体磁捕获电化学测定法,用于检测人工唾液中的乙型流感病毒(IBV)和人 呼吸道合胞病毒(hRSV)。对于每种目标病毒,使用两个序列不同的DNA适体:氨基修饰的捕获适体(IBV1或RSV1)通过与聚多巴胺醌/儿茶酚表面的直接席夫碱反应共价偶联至~5μm聚多巴胺包被的磁性微粒,以及硫醇修饰的检测适体(IBV2或RSV2)通过丝网印刷金电极自组装硫醇-金化学。在使用两种适体磁性颗粒类型进行单一多重批量捕获步骤后,将颗粒分开并通过方波伏安法 (SWV) 在两个适体修饰的电极上并行分析。SWV 校准曲线的 Langmuir 分析得出表观解离常数 Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1 (IBV) 和 226 ± 85 PFU mL-1 (hRSV),检测限分别为 15 和 11 PFU mL-1。对数线性校准在两个通道上的范围为 101-104 PFU mL-1(n = 4 个浓度,R2 = 0.995 和 0.990),灵敏度为每十年 8.58 和 6.61 μA,因此每个病毒特异性检测涵盖三个数量级的病毒载量。序列-正交双适体几何结构-针对不同表位的捕获和检测识别-被提议作为结构缓解。这一概念验证建立了一种可编程的、唾液兼容的架构,可仅通过适体替换来针对新出现的呼吸道病原体进行重新配置。

papers.title: Temporal Patterns and Distribution of Laboratory-Confirmed Respiratory Pathogen Detections in a Tertiary Hospital in Southern Brazil (2023–2026)
papers.abstract: Objective: To describe the epidemiological, clinical, and seasonal patterns of respiratory viral infections in Southern Brazil between January 2023 and April 2026. Methods: A retrospective observational descriptive study was conducted at a private hospital including laboratory-confirmed cases of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (H3N2 and H1N1), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV A and B), rhinovirus, adenovirus, metapneumovirus, enterovirus, bocavirus, parainfluenza viruses, and seasonal coronaviruses. Respiratory pathogens were detected using molecular testing (XGEN MULTI PR24 FLOW CHIP) or rapid antigen detection tests. Demographic, clinical, and temporal data were analyzed according to age group. Results: A total of 18,214 detections were identified. Influenza A was the most frequent pathogen (48.08%), followed by SARS-CoV-2 (23.73%) and RSV A (8.65%). Hospitalization occurred in 20.44% of patients, 21.11% of hospitalized individuals required intensive care, and 2.93% required mechanical ventilation. Adults showed alternating seasonal peaks of influenza A and SARS-CoV-2, with influenza A predominating during colder seasons and SARS-CoV-2 during warmer periods. In children, SARS-CoV-2 incidence was lower, whereas RSV A and other respiratory viruses showed greater circulation. Declines in influenza A and COVID-19 detections were observed during periods that temporally overlapped with national vaccination campaigns; however, vaccination coverage was not assessed in this study. Conclusions: Respiratory viral infections remained frequent in the post-pandemic period, reinforcing the importance of continuous surveillance, seasonal monitoring, and vaccination strategies.

papers.title: Effects of different doses of Poly I:C on immune responses and protective efficacy induced by intranasal immunization with HRSV pre-F protein in mice
papers.abstract: Background Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) primarily infects the respiratory mucosa, making local mucosal immunity an important target for vaccine development. Poly I:C is a promising mucosal adjuvant, but the effects of different doses on immune responses and protection induced by intranasal HRSV prefusion F (Pre-F) protein vaccination remain unclear. Methods Female BALB/c mice were assigned to five groups ( n = 6 per group): Pre-F + 10 μg CpG, Pre-F + 10 μg Poly I:C, Pre-F + 25 μg Poly I:C, Pre-F + 50 μg Poly I:C, and PBS. Mice were immunized intranasally on days 0 and 21. Serum Pre-F-specific antibodies and HRSV-neutralizing antibodies were measured after the second immunization. Mice were challenged intranasally with HRSV Long strain 14 days after the second immunization. Body weight, splenic cytokine-secreting lymphocytes, lung Pre-F-specific IgA, HRSV RNA loads, and lung histopathology were evaluated. Results All immunized groups developed Pre-F-specific antibody responses. Neutralizing antibody titers in the 10, 25, and 50 μg Poly I:C groups were 262, 340, and 1,173, respectively, while lung Pre-F-specific IgA titers were 1,185, 1,405, and 1,838. All Poly I:C groups induced IFN- γ -secreting lymphocyte responses, with the strongest response observed in the 50 μg group. Following HRSV challenge, immunized mice showed less body weight loss, lower lung HRSV RNA loads, and reduced histopathological injury than PBS controls. Among the Poly I:C groups, the 50 μg group had the lowest lung HRSV RNA load (30.6 copies/mg), approximately 1/25 of that in the PBS group (766.5 copies/mg). Conclusion Poly I:C enhanced systemic, mucosal, and cellular immune responses induced by intranasal HRSV Pre-F immunization and improved protection against HRSV challenge. Within the tested dose range, 50 μg Poly I:C showed the most favorable overall profile among the Poly I:C groups and warrants further dose-optimization and safety evaluation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effects of different doses of Poly I:C on immune responses and protective efficacy induced by intranasal immunization with HRSV pre-F protein in mice. The study design involved five groups of mice, each receiving different combinations of HRSV Pre-F protein and adjuvants. Results showed that all immunized groups developed Pre-F-specific antibody responses, with the 50 μg Poly I:C group demonstrating the strongest neutralizing antibody titers and lung Pre-F-specific IgA levels. The authors concluded that Poly I:C enhances immune responses and improves protection against HRSV challenge. The study's findings suggest that Poly I:C could be a valuable adjuvant for HRSV vaccine development. However, the study was conducted in mice, and further research is needed to evaluate its efficacy and safety in humans.

All Poly I:C groups induced IFN- γ -secreting lymphocyte responses, with the strongest response observed in the 50 μg group. Following HRSV challenge, immunized mice showed less body weight loss, lower lung HRSV RNA loads, and reduced histopathological injury than PBS controls. Among the Poly I:C groups, the 50 μg group had the lowest lung HRSV RNA load (30.6 copies/mg), approximately 1/25 of that in the PBS group (766.5 copies/mg). Conclusion Poly I:C enhanced systemic, mucosal, and cellular immune responses induced by intranasal HRSV Pre-F immunization and improved protection against HRSV challenge. Within the tested dose range, 50 μg Poly I:C showed the most favorable overall profile among the Poly I:C groups and warrants further dose-optimization and safety evaluation.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 雌性BALB/c小鼠被分为五组(每组n=6):Pre-F + 10 μg CpG,Pre-F + 10 μg Poly I:C,Pre-F + 25 μg Poly I:C,Pre-F + 50 μg Poly I:C,以及PBS。
analysis_zh.methods: 在第二次免疫后检测血清Pre-F特异性抗体和HRSV中和抗体。小鼠在第0天和第21天进行鼻内免疫。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: Poly I:C增强了鼻内接种HRSV Pre-F蛋白诱导的全身性、黏膜性和细胞性免疫应答,并提高了对HRSV挑战的保护效果。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,Poly I:C可以作为佐剂用于提高鼻内接种HRSV Pre-F蛋白的保护效果,这可能为疫苗的开发策略提供参考。
